text:
## Abstract
This study quantifies the fraction of Escherichia coli sequencing runs in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) that mention "carbapenem" in their study titles. The ENA database was queried using the taxonomic identifier for E. coli and the keyword "carbapenem" in the study title. Among 551,679 total E. coli runs, 9,759 runs mention "carbapenem," resulting in an estimated fraction of approximately 1.77%. This fraction reflects research interest and data availability regarding carbapenem resistance or exposure in E. coli. This measure provides insight into the relative volume of sequencing data focusing on carbapenem-related studies, important for antimicrobial resistance surveillance.

## I. Introduction
Background: Escherichia coli, a widespread bacterial species, is a major cause of infections in humans and animals. Carbapenems are a class of last-resort antibiotics used to treat multidrug-resistant infections. The emergence of carbapenem-resistant E. coli is a critical concern in public health.

Literature Review: No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap: The proportion of E. coli sequencing data specifically associated with carbapenem-related studies in public repositories was not quantified.

Objective & Hypothesis: To determine the fraction of E. coli ENA sequencing runs linked to studies that mention "carbapenem," we expect a measurable portion to be associated due to rising research attention on resistance.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design: Public sequencing run metadata from the ENA database were analyzed. Two queries were performed: one to retrieve the total number of E. coli runs and one for runs mentioning "carbapenem" in the study title.

Materials: ENA accessed through BRC Analytics ENA search tool.

Procedures: 
- Query 1: Search for all sequencing runs with taxon ID 562 (E. coli), limit 20 for example but total returned.
- Query 2: Search for runs with taxon ID 562 and study title containing "carbapenem".
- Extract total counts of matched runs from metadata.

Statistical Analysis: The fraction was computed by dividing the number of carbapenem-related runs by the total number of E. coli runs.

## III. Results

| Query Description               | Number of Runs    |
|-------------------------------|------------------|
| Total E. coli runs              | 551,679          |
| Runs mentioning "carbapenem"   | 9,759            |
| Fraction (carbapenem/total)    | 0.0177 (1.77%)   |

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation: Approximately 1.77% of all E. coli sequencing runs in ENA are associated with studies mentioning carbapenem in their titles, indicating a significant focus on carbapenem-related research.

Context: The returned count of 9,759 carbapenem-related runs reflects the growing global surveillance and study of carbapenem resistance in E. coli using sequencing.

Limitations: The search uses study title keywords only, which may miss relevant data in studies not mentioning carbapenem explicitly in the title. The database updates continuously so these numbers are snapshots.

Conclusion & Future Directions: This analysis provides a baseline fraction of carbapenem-related E. coli data in ENA. Future work could refine the search by searching sample or experiment metadata to capture broader datasets.

## References
[1] European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) run metadata: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?query=scientific_name=%22Escherichia coli%22%20AND%20study_title=%22*carbapenem*%22  
[2] European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) run metadata: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?query=tax_eq(562)

## Acknowledgments
Data providers: European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and BRC Analytics for access to sequencing run metadata.
